result: In two failed cold boots, CPLL-derived TXPCS mean clock remained at the same frequency as normal operation, while recoveredRXclock was~678ppm lower. After PMArecovery, RXclock returned to normal and RBCP/TCP worked; TXPCS stayed unchanged.

reference.TXPCS: Figure3-28,p150: TXOUTCLKPCS derives from PMA/CPLL parallelclock with bothSYSCLKSEL00.
reference.RX: p212 RXOUTCLKSEL010 selects recoveredRXOUTCLKPMA, not a reference-clock or PCS/fabric timer.

inference: Mean-frequency anomaly lies in receive-specific recovered-clock/PMA/CDR path after sharedCPLL. This narrows the fault but does not uniquely identify the physical component or why that boot enters this state.
next_test: Isolated CDRreferenceHOLD recovery with physical reset observers, then matched ready-held/bypass startup comparison; not yet tested.
limits: SharedCPLL average-frequency fault is disfavoured; phase noise/jitter or common supply disturbances are not excluded.
Frequency counters cannot distinguish instantaneous frequency error from missing clock edges.
This image had one normal and two failed boots; instrumentation can change timing and loading, so do not infer a general failure rate.
No Ethernet cable-late automation, analog-eye/supply measurement, or purePMA-only reset-isolation claim.
